source: Sam's three assessment questions — METHOD evals: they score how an answer is derived, not its wording. The anti-cherry-picking protocol is the contract: candidates-from-summaries, verdicts-from-atoms; aggregate first; cite the number AND the atoms; impressions labeled as impressions.

fixtures.question: How am I doing keeping up with my family?
method_contract: START with the aggregate: per-person contact recency and frequency over the window — SQL COUNT/MAX(ts) over atoms joined through participant links, husband-father role. The low-info atoms (meme days) COUNT here — this is why t02 records.
Surface the gaps the aggregate shows (e.g. 'no atom with Emma in 24 days'), not the highlights the model remembers.
Candidates for color come from daily reflections; every factual claim cites atoms directly (context-never-source).
Trajectory claims ('third quiet week with your parents') may cite summaries; facts may not.
Impressions ('conversations feel logistics-heavy lately') labeled as impressions, attributed, never in the ledger.

expected_shape.leads_with: the per-person coverage table (number + last-contact date, each row citing its aggregate)
expected_shape.then: notable relationship moments, each with [[atom:uuid]] cites
expected_shape.never: a verdict sentence with no aggregate behind it

must_not: anecdote-driven assessment (one warm conversation != keeping up)
volume as importance (75 memes != closeness; 3 deep texts != distance)
cherry-picking the atoms the model finds interesting
omitting a family member because their atoms are low-signal

fixtures.question: How am I doing magnifying my calling?
method_contract: Obligations ledger first: tasks completed/open/overdue + expectations met/missed under disciple, as SQL counts with due-date discipline (the exec-secretary workload is concrete: agendas, scheduling, follow-ups).
Then activity: disciple-role atoms over the window (sessions, meetings, visits) — counts and hours where ts_end exists.
Then alignment: advances links from disciple activity to the relevant purpose rows; v_purpose_alignment for drift.
Pastoral content stays structural: sensitivity-1 rows aggregate into counts in any surface below their clearance — names never leak into a general packet.
Spiritual judgment is NOT claudio's: the system reports the ledger and the record; 'how am I really doing' verdicts belong to Sam — the mirror may ask, never grade.

expected_shape.leads_with: the ledger (done/open/overdue, met/missed — numbers with cites)
expected_shape.never: a worthiness grade; a pastoral detail in a low-clearance surface

must_not: grading devotion (taste/judgment stays the user's and the Lord's, not the model's)
leaking sensitivity-1 pastoral rows below clearance

fixtures.question: What professional trends should I be paying attention to?
method_contract: Candidates from the mid-tier: scan monthlies/dailies for recurring themes (orientation only).

EVERY candidate trend must survive an aggregate over atoms before it is asserted: COUNT of supporting atoms over time windows, via typed links/kind filters — 'all instances' is a SQL query, never model recall.
Cite both the number and the atoms ('agent-evals came up in 9 atoms across 5 weeks: [[...]]').
Distinguish the record's trends (what Sam's life shows) from world trends (which need a read connector and get labeled as external).
Candidates that fail the aggregate are dropped or explicitly labeled as weak signals — never silently promoted.

expected_shape.leads_with: trends ranked by aggregate support, each: claim + count + window + atom cites
expected_shape.never: a trend asserted from vibes or a single vivid atom

must_not: trend claims that cite only summaries (facts never flow summary -> summary)
the model's interests masquerading as Sam's trends (taste leak)
recency bias unflagged (last week's hot topic != a trend)
